subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend boundary that can route finished recordings through Gateway media-audio or another approved ASR contract, and what security/fallback policy should it use?
rationale: The code confirms the missing capability, but implementing it safely requires maintainer intent on native-app versus Gateway ownership, provider credentials, private-network access, fallback behavior, and how this narrower PTT slice relates to the broader custom ASR issue.

options.title: Design batch PTT seam first
options.body: Approve a narrow batch-only PTT backend abstraction that preserves Apple Speech by default and reuses existing media-audio/provider contracts where possible.

options.title: Fold into broad custom ASR design
options.body: Keep this as context under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and decide all native voice ASR surfaces together before any implementation.

options.title: Defer custom native STT
options.body: Keep platform Speech as the only native PTT transcription path until the provider and security model is clearer.

recommendation.title: Design batch PTT seam first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow batch-only PTT backend abstraction that preserves Apple Speech by default and reuses existing media-audio/provider contracts where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: The central code path is native macOS voice/PTT, where Peter Steinberger has the strongest sampled feature-history signal.
